title: tooling(pm): three ordered read paths for check-clause2-carriers, so a seat's ACCESS stops deciding whether clause-② is checkable
body:
Part of #14965 — the TOOLING half (direction A) only. The claim-template half is a separate branch and is not addressed here.

## What changed

`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` now reads a pair down a **declared ladder** instead of one path, and reports which rung answered: **(i)** `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` when the environment exports one — still the first choice, the largest budget and the only path that can read a private board, except that a credential the API *refuses* (401/403) is now retired for the rest of the run instead of failing the read, because a stale token must never make a **public** pair unreadable; **(ii)** the same request with no `authorization` header, which these public boards serve — the reader always omitted the header when no token was exported, so what is new is that this path is declared, reachable as a fallback from a refused credential, and reported; **(iii)** `--pair-json FILE` (or `--pair-json -` for stdin) — the pair pre-fetched into a document and judged with **no network at all**, which is the path an MCP-only seat has, and a named document is the WHOLE input, never half a document and half a live board.

Judging is untouched: the closed `yes`/`no` vocabulary, `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE` / `CLAUSE2_NEAR_MISS_LINE`, the four-valued read (`malformed` / `misplaced` / `absent` / `unreadable`), the carrier set and the exit register 0/2/3/4 all keep their meanings. The document path is deliberately **asymmetric**: a key the document omits reads `null`, which every caller already treats as UNJUDGED, so a hand-assembled input can only make this file say *less* about a pair, never more. Every refusal now names which paths were tried, and every run prints the `x-ratelimit-remaining` it actually saw.

## The premise, re-measured — and the half of it that was wrong

The card's premise is that the checker "needs its own token and exits 2". Read against the tree, **the reader never checked for a token**: it already omitted the header when none was exported. Measured from this container, 2026-09-04:

- a header-less `GET /repos/…/pulls/15460` → **HTTP 200**, with `x-ratelimit-limit: 15000`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 14576`, `x-ratelimit-used: 424`, `x-ratelimit-resource: core`;
- the **unmodified** script with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GH_TOKEN` unset → `--pair 15460` exits **0**, the same verdicts as the token run.

But 15000 is not the anonymous budget. GitHub documents 60/hour per IP for anonymous core, and a header-less `GET /user` from this container answers **with an identity**; the egress proxy also **overrides** an `authorization` header the caller sends (a deliberately invalid token still reads 200 as that identity). So "token-less reads work here" is true and "these reads are anonymous" is not — both regimes are in play depending on where the checker runs, which is exactly why the run now prints the remaining count it saw instead of stating a budget it did not measure. That override is also why the token-retirement rung cannot be produced natively in this container and was proved with a harness instead (row G below).

Direction A's real gap was therefore not a token check. It was (a) no offline path at all for a seat with no network, (b) a refusal that did not say which paths had been tried, and (c) a budget nobody printed. This PR closes those three.

## Test matrix

All rows at `20c27b3ef`; each exit code captured before any pipe.

| # | run | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| — | `pnpm check:pm-clause2-carriers` (the file's own self-test, offline) | **0** — 174 cases (150 pre-existing + 24 new), new battery pinned at its landed floor, roster size floor raised with it |
| A | `--pair 15460`, token exported | **0** — 4 pairs legible; report: token served 9 reads, `rate limit seen (core): 14404 of 15000 remaining` |
| B | `--pair 15460`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` unset | **0** — same 4 verdicts; report: token-less public read served 9 reads |
| G | `--pair 15460`, token exported, harness answering 403 to any request carrying `authorization` (header-less requests reach the real API) | **0** — one `token … was refused (HTTP 403); falling back` line, then the public read carries the run; report: `token: present but REFUSED (HTTP 403) — retired for the rest of this run` |
| C | `--pair 15460 --pair-json pair.json`, no token | **0** — same 4 verdicts; report: document served 9 reads, public read 0 |
| C2 | the same document on **stdin** (`--pair-json -`) | **0** — identical verdicts, `read from stdin` |
| C3 | C with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a thrower, inherited through `NODE_OPTIONS` so the proxy re-exec inherits it too | **0** — identical verdicts with **provably zero** network reads |
| ctrl | the positive control for C3: the same stub, **no** document | **3** — PREREQUISITE NOT MET, and the read-path line names the `--pair-json` remedy. (The first attempt at this control passed for the wrong reason — `--import` did not survive the script's proxy re-exec — which is why the stub is injected through `NODE_OPTIONS`.) |
| E | `--pair` on a merged PR (pair cannot be formed) | **2** — unchanged wording, plus "which reads were tried, and on which path, is the line below" and the path report |

The offline rows judge the *same* pair as the live rows and return the *same* verdicts, which is the property that matters: path (iii) is not a second reader, it is the same predicates fed from a document.

## Gates

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran ran.list` → exit 0: **"✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 25 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 25 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED."** Re-derived after `git fetch origin main`: same 25. Every one of the 25 exited 0 (slowest: `check:pm-dispatch-gates`, 329 s).
- Also run, because their rosters sit under `scripts/` or `scripts/pm/` and the derivation marks their silence as evidence in neither direction: `check:pm-label-desc-cap`, `check:pm-governed-prose`, `check:pm-skill-ratchet`, `check-published-list-mirrors.mjs` — all exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` → exit 0: **"NOT governed — ordinary queue landing applies to a PR with exactly this file list."**
- Lint is a **declared narrowing**, not a skip: `eslint scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --no-inline-config --format json` → exit 0, and the JSON reports **1 file linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings**. The file is inside eslint's own configured population (`--print-config` resolves rules for it rather than reporting it ignored), and the flat config enables **no** type-aware linting for any file — no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`, which the config says of itself at `eslint.config.mjs:326` — so this diff cannot move the verdict on a file it does not touch. The repo-wide scan is CI's run.
- `grep -naP` for control characters over the changed file: no hits; `check:nul-bytes` green in the union above.

## Scope

One file: `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`. No `.claude/**`, no `skills/**`, no `AGENTS.md`, no other script, no changeset (an internal PM gate publishes nothing) — hence `skip-changeset`.
